subject: biology
title: Cardiac Output & Blood
welcome_lead: Today you'll calculate cardiac output and read what a blood test really tells you.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology cardiac output equation, blood test interpretation, blood group basics.
final_note: You learned the cardiac output equation, what blood cell counts mean, and basic blood-group rules.

concepts.def: Volume of blood pumped per minute by the heart
Volume of blood pumped per single heartbeat
Cell that fights infection — pathogens and viruses
Cell fragment that helps blood clot at a wound
Group O blood — can be given to any recipient

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume.

Heart rate is beats per minute. Stroke volume is mL pumped per beat. Multiply them for the total mL pumped per minute.

If two values are given, rearrange the equation to find the third — like density or speed problems.

Red cell count low? Likely anaemia — less oxygen carried.

White cell count high? Body is fighting an infection.

Platelet count low? Blood clots too slowly — bruising and bleeding.

You can be group A, B, AB or O.

Group O has no A or B markers — so it can be donated to anyone. That makes it the universal donor.

Group AB can accept any group — it is the universal recipient.
